question.text:
X , . . . , X are independent with common variance 1. Let A = (X + · · · + X )/10 and
1 15 1 10
B = (X + · · · + X )/10. What is Var(A − B)?
6 15
(A) 1/20 (B) 1/10 (C) 3/20 (D) 1/5 (E) 1/2

solution.text:
The five shared variables cancel. The difference is 1/10 times five independent variables
minus five other independent variables. Hence its variance is 10/100 = 1/10. Equivalently
Cov(A, B) = 5/100.

question.text:
Let Y equal zero or one with probability 1/2 each, and set X = Y for every i. Which pair gives
i
Var(X ) and P (|X − 1/2| > 1/4)?
n n
(A) (1/(4n), 0) (B) (1/4, 1) (C) (1/(4n), 1/2) (D) (1/4, 1/2) (E) (0, 0)

solution.text:
The observations are identical, not independent, so their average is exactly Y for every sam-
ple size. Its variance stays 1/4, and its distance from 1/2 is always 1/2, giving probability
one. Averaging alone does not force concentration or justify a central-limit approximation.
Covariance terms exactly offset the usual independent-sample variance reduction.
